=== CONTEXT (do NOT extract rows from this part; use only to identify the section headers in effect) ===
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Secretary, Civil Service Commission.
CIVIL SERVICE COMMISSION, February 11, 1924.

SIR, - I beg to acknowledge receipt of your letter of the 5th instant with reference to the case of Mr. J.R. McGregor,
Indian Agent, Grade 4, at Gore Bay, Ont. The salary increases effective 1st April, 1922, and 1st April, 1923, to which
reference is made in your letter, were approved by the Civil Service Commission on the understanding that
Mr. McGregor was a permanent employee within the meaning of the definition of a permanent employee given by the
Department of Justice, the Department of Indian Affairs having informed the Commission that all the Indian Agents
had been regularly appointed to permanent positions by competent authority.

It was only after the salary increases had been approved that Mr. McGregor's temporary status was learned through the
recommendation of the Department that he be made permanent under the provisions of P.C. 2958. As Mr. McGregor
can only be considered as a temporary employee up to the date when he was made permanent under the blanketing
regulations, I am inclined to agree with you that the salary increases granted on the 1st April, 1922, and 1st April,
1923, were not legally authorized by the terms of the Civil Service Act and that Mr. McGregor was only entitled
therefore to receive on permanent appointment a salary rate, of $1,440 per annum.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. FORAN, Secretary.


The Assistant Auditor General.

<!-- page 549 -->
AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, February 19, 1924.

SIR, - On December 24th last an Order in Council (P.C. 60/2521) was passed, based on a report. from the Civil
Service Commission, granting permanent status from April 1st, 1923, to a number of employees of your department.
Among the employees so blanketed in I find the Dame of Mr. J.R. McGregor, Indian Agent, grade 4, at Gore Bay, Ont.

Mr. McGregor was first employed as agent on July 4th, 1916, at a salary of $800, and continued to be paid at that rate
until the reclassification, when, the position being classified as Indian Agent, grade 4, his salary was raised to $1,440,
the minimum of the class, from April 1st, 1919. Mr. McGregor's salary remained at $1,440 until April 1st, 1922, when
it was raised to $1,560 (the next step) under the authority of a certificate issued by the Civil Service Commission on
May 11th, 1922, and a further increase to $1,680 was made on April 1st, 1923, under the authority of a certificate
issued on February 21st, 1923.

On my pointing out to the Civil Service Commission that, in my opinion, if Mr. McGregor was considered a temporary
employee only until the passing of the Order in Council of December 24th, he was not legally entitled to receive the
increases granted on April 14, 1922, and on April 1st, 1923, and that, accordingly, his permanency should be only at
the salary to which he was legally entitled, viz., $1,440, the secretary of the Commission replied as follows:

"It was only after the salary increases had been approved that Mr. McGregor's temporary status was learned through
the recommendation of the Department. that he be made permanent under the provisions of P.C. 2958. As
Mr. McGregor can only be considered as a temporary employee up to the date when he was made permanent under the
blanketing regulations, I am inclined to agree with you that the salary increases granted on the 1st April, 1922, and
1st April, 1923, were not legally authorized by the terms of the Civil Service Act and that Mr. McGregor was only
entitled, therefore, to receive on permanent appointment a salary rate of $1,440 per annum."

I shall be glad to be informed as to any action that you may propose to take in this ease.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G.

The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.
DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, May 9, 1924.

SIR, - With reference to your letter of the 19th February last, respecting the salary paid to Mr. J.R. McGregor, Indian
Agent, Gore Bay, Ont., since the 1st April, 1922, I beg to say that this question was taken up with the Civil Service
Commission with the result that a joint memorandum was submitted to the Treasury Board recommending that
Mr. McGregor's permanency date from the 1st April, 1921. The Secretary to the Treasury Board informs me that the
Board, at a meeting held on the 1st instant, had under consideration the recommendation referred to, but they decided
that recommendations of this nature shall not be made effective prior to the 1st of April of the then current fiscal year
and, accordingly, did not recommend this report for the favourable consideration of Council.

In view of the Board's decision, Mr. McGregor has been overpaid $120 during the fiscal year 1922 - 23, $240 in 1923 -
24 and $20 for April of this fiscal year, making a total overpayment of $380 to the 30th April last. Against this,
however, Mr. McGregor would have been entitled to $59 more bonus during

1 - 13I

<!-- page 550 -->
1922 - 23 and $110 more in 1923 - 24, making a total of $170, which if deducted from the overpayment of $380 made
to him, would leave a net overpayment of $210, It is not permissible, however, I understand, to pay bonus for last year
from the current year's bonus appropriation, so that the overpayment of $380 would not be reduced from that source.

As it would be a hardship to call upon Mr. McGregor to refund an overpayment of $380 for which he is in no wise
responsible I trust that some way out will be found so that he will not be called-upon to do so.


Your obedient servant,
D.C. SCOTT, D.S.G.


The Auditor General.

Vote 274, Indians of Ontario and Quebec: Payments to Salaried Physician for Special Medical Services


AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, May 3, 1924.

SIR, - Dr. W.H. Woods of Mount Brydges, Ont., has been employed for some years as Indian Physician, part time, at a
salary of $1,700 per annum. During the fiscal year 1922 - 23 and 1923 - 24 he was paid the following amounts, in
addition to his salary, for special medical services rendered the Indians,: -

1922 - 23 Cheque No. 938, Ontario and Quebec Vote $180 50
1922 - 23 Cheque No. 267, Education Vote          76 00
1923 - 24 Cheque No. 1056, Education Vote         150 00
Total                                             $406 50

The classification schedule gives the following as the compensation for the position of Physician.

"Compensation. Up to $175 per month for part time service, depending upon the time required, the population, and
local conditions. For the present existing rates shall continue; in case of a new appointment, or in case an adjustment
becomes necessary, the value of the duties performed shall be appraised by the department and the Civil Service
Commission." In view of the foregoing I am of the opinion that these payments to Dr. Woods, over and above his
salary, for special services. should not have been made without the approval of the Civil Service Commission.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM, KEARNS, Asst. A.G.


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


Vote 275, Indians of Manitoba, etc.: Payments by Indian Agent in Advance of Receipt of Funds from
Department

AUDITOR GENERAL'S OFFICE, February 13, 1924.

SIR, - On April 23, 1923, cheque No. 51 for $400 was issued against your Manitoba and North West Vote in favour of
R.E. Osborn, Indian agent at Broadview, "In Trust" as an advance for repairs, to the Crooked Lake Agency house. This
cheque was received by Mr. Osborn on April 28th, and was, I presume, placed to the credit of his Trust Account on
that day. According to the receipts submitted by Mr. Osborn in support of his expenditure under this. advance, the

<!-- page 551 -->
following payments were made by him to, Mr. J. Woodward: -

<!-- page 552 -->
April 24th, On Account of wages, repairs to Agency house                 $130 00
May 5th, Wages, Buildings account                                        75 00
May 5th, Wages, on account Agency House, repairs (paid to Mrs. Woodward) 25 00
May 12th, Wages, on account Building, Repairs to Agency house            50 00
May 22nd, Repairs to Agency house, Building Account                      120 00
Total                                                                    $400 00

It does not appear from these receipts whether Mr. Woodward was, employed on the repairs at a daily rate of wages or
was allowed the round sum of $400 for the job. If the former, a statement should be submitted by the agent stating the
rate paid per them and the number of days employed, if the latter, a copy of the agreement entered into with
Mr. Woodward should be furnished me.

It will be noticed that the first payment to Mr. Woodward was one of $130 made on April 24th, four days before the
agent received the advance from your department. This first payment must, no doubt, have been made from
Mr. Osborn's Trust Account, out of moneys placed in that account for other purposes. I beg to remind you that, as I
stated in my letter of June 22nd, 1923, with regard to a somewhat similar case at the Blackfoot Agency, the diversion
of Trust Funds, even temporarily, for any purpose other than that for which they are held is a practice that should not
be allowed in any case, but such Trust Funds should be guarded jealously for the special purpose for which they were
placed in trust.


I am, sir, your obedient servant,
WM. KEARNS, Asst. A.G


The Deputy Superintendent General of Indian Affairs.


DEPARTMENT OF INDIAN AFFAIRS, March 14, 1924.

SIR, - Referring to your letter of the 13th ultimo, regarding cheque No. 51 for $400 issued on April 23rd, 1923, against
our Manitoba and North West Vote in favour of Mr. R.E. Osborn, In Trust, as an advance for repairs to the Crooked
Lake Agency house, I beg to quote the following explanation furnished by Mr. Osborn in regard to the last paragraph
of your letter, viz.: -

"On April 23rd, 1923, an accountable advance cheque for $300 was received from Commissioner Graham to, apply on
the Woodward contract and on the 24th April the payment of $130 referred to in your letter was paid Mr. Woodward
from this $300.

"Accountable cheque No. 51 for $400 from the Department was received on the 28th April and on the same day a
cheque for $300 was sent to Commissioner Graham to refund the amount received from him on the 23rd thus making
the $130 chargeable to cheque No. 51.

"It will be seen from this that no Trust funds were used to pay Mr Woodward."

With regard to the agreement entered into, with Mr. J. Woodward, I beg to state that a copy was sent to your office by
the Department on the 6th November last, but I herewith enclose another copy.


Your obedient servant,
J.D. McLEAN, Asst. Deputy.
